intervals.label: LST sub-array (LST-1 to LST-4, CTAO-North) completed and inaugurated
intervals.note: CTAO press release, La Palma, 15 October 2026: 250 scientists "celebrated the inauguration of the Large-Sized Telescope (LST) sub-array at the CTAO-North site"; "The completion of the four telescopes marks a significant milestone ... and represents a crucial step toward the full scientific operation" of CTAO; "With the three new LSTs (LST-2, LST-3, and LST-4) joining the existing LST-1, the four telescopes will become a true array"; "Over the coming years, the LSTs will undergo commissioning and integration into CTAO operations." LST-1, the prototype, has produced 'groundbreaking results since 2020', even during its commissioning phase. Recorded as a milestone annotation (kind phase) and not as a commissioning interval: the Atlas holds one aggregate record for the whole observatory (both sites, all telescope classes), not one per telescope, the article gives no commissioning dates for LST-2 to LST-4 and says commissioning is still ahead, and the rest of CTAO (MSTs, SSTs, CTAO-South) remains under construction. The observatory-level status stays `construction`.

summary.plain: Two big groups of gamma-ray telescopes, one in Spain and one in Chile, coming in three different sizes so together they can see the whole range of gamma-ray energies.
summary.technical: Imaging-atmospheric-Cherenkov arrays at two sites (La Palma / Paranal), using Large-, Medium- and Small-Sized Telescope classes (design maximum 4 LST + 23 MST + 37 SST) to cover 20 GeV-300 TeV; under construction as of 2026-10-25 (CTAO press release of 2026-10-15 on the completed LST sub-array).

technology.value: Two ground-based arrays of imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes in three size classes (Large, Medium, Small).
